evidence: paper: c_{i_0} N_{i_0} \Delta v = -E_\theta^{\circ}, \qquad c_{i_0} N_{i_0} \Delta\gamma = -E_z^{\circ} + \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ax}}, \qquad \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ax}} = c_{i_0} N_{i_0} (\Delta\gamma - \gamma_d)

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Both identities are stated, in the form c N (.) rather than with c N moved to the left-hand side: fastAtIndex h n i is the Lean's c_{i0} N_{i0} (it multiplies by Tg^i Q_n^{1+h} and applies graphDz, the inverse pairing being temporalAtIndex_fast_cancellation). The first conjunct of commonTemporalFields_fast_cancellation is c N (Delta v) + E_theta^o = 0, the paper's first identity. The second is c N (Delta gamma) + E_z^o = -c N (alias), and commonTemporalFields_axial_eq gives Delta gamma = gamma_d - alias, so -c N (alias) = c N (Delta gamma - gamma_d) = F_ax; the paper's second and third identities are that one equation read with F_ax named. The sign convention is the only rewriting: the Lean's named alias carries the minus sign that the paper absorbs into F_ax (VariableGaugeMean.temporalAliasState stores -fastTime applied to gamma_d - Delta gamma). I verified the identities as stated; I did not trace which of the MeanChartCompatibility and VariableGaugeMean copies the Proposition 9.6 chain actually invokes.
